T-001.Title: Widen kind union and payer filter; isolated kind, ceiling, and window fixtures

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Amend scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts and scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts. Do not write production registry.xml or invoke production --retire. RegistryRow.kind at scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:69 becomes "chartered" | "sweep-remainder" | "historical". The XML payer-row collector currently named charteredRowsFromRoot (:731) includes kind="historical" alongside kind="chartered" (a rename of the function is allowed, not required). kind="sweep-remainder" stays out of the payer map. A Row whose kind is not in that closed union, live or retired, is a validator error: the non-mutating validate run exits non-zero and the message names the illegal kind value, so a typo cannot go silent-invisible. derivePayerMap (:444) is otherwise unchanged: it still requires archive.has(row.name), still reads Pays F-tokens first, still reads Closed with tokens from StatusText, still reads the archived-spec payer phrase. It does not grow a /delivered|superseded/i filter on StatusText. Tests import median from scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts; do not re-implement it. Do not add a ngrace lint issue code. Do not edit src/, skills/ngrace/*, or the packaged mirror.

Isolated fixtures, argv naming a fixture directory so they do not read or write the repository record files. (1) kind="historical": a fixture registry row with kind="historical", name equal to an archive directory, Pays naming a live finding token, and StatusText that does not match /delivered|superseded/i, appears in the payer map and makes that finding eligible. The same fixture with kind="sweep-remainder" and the same Pays does not. A kind="chartered" row still pays as today. A Row whose kind is not in the closed union (for example kind="history" or kind="Historical") makes the non-mutating validate run exit non-zero. (2) ceiling-order: an isolated fixture whose live registry snapshot matches the production ceiling formula, with the pre-insert live row count plus four historical archive-named rows still less than or equal to the persisted ceiling, observes the live registry file after insert and before --retire so the order is not vacuous, then --retire persists that ceiling, returns live occupancy to the pre-insert count, and places the four rows in the retired sibling. A write that planted the rows directly in the retired sibling fails this probe. (3) window-fuel: an isolated fixture --retire that moves finding elements paid by historical archive-named rows opens a findings window of H + Delta_retired under the shipped C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW formula (ceiling stays the previously persisted value when Base_live + H meets or exceeds it; base drops by the moved lines; headroom = ceiling - base). After this task, bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts on the production record still exits 0 and live registry occupancy is still the pre-insert count.

T-002.Title: Insert four historical rows and --retire in the same wave

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Insert four historical rows into live production registry.xml, then invoke one bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire against the production record (no fixture argv) in this same task, before any commit validate:ci can see. Do not separate the insert and the --retire into two tasks or two commits: after insert the four names equal archive directories, so they are immediately registry-eligible, and T-001's widened filter makes the paid findings immediately finding-eligible; a commit or a task boundary holding that tree fails registry-eligible-still-live and finding-eligible-still-live. The intermediate occupancy 11+4=15 does not exceed ceiling 26 (live-row units, checkCeilingValue at scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1233); that is why the ceiling is not the reason they cannot be separated — eligibility is. One --retire pass, not two: retireRecord stamps <PaidBy> onto eligible live findings and moves those findings and the archive-named rows in one invocation (findings move by derived payer token; rows move because name equals an archive directory, independent of kind). A second production --retire after the move writes no byte. Do not hand-edit <PaidBy>. Do not write the rows directly into registry-retired.xml. Do not raise the persisted ceiling. Do not flush .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md. Do not mint a chartered row for C-PAYMENT-RECORD.
